---
title: "check-rubric-checklists.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that warns when a pull request adds or revises
a grading rubric that is not written as a checklist.
The lab's default (Ezra, 2026-10-27) is that most STEM grading rubrics are checklists:
one item per observable criterion, so a grader marks each item as earned or not.

A rubric is a line that opens with `Grading`, `Rubric`, `Marking scheme` or `Mark scheme`,
bare, bolded, in a blockquote or as a heading,
followed by `(`, `:` or the end of the line.
Its block is that line plus the blank lines, list items and indented lines after it.
The check reports a rubric whose block holds no task-list item (`- [ ] ...`).

The check does not count:

- anything inside a code fence or an HTML comment;
- a rubric that carries `<!-- rubric-ok: reason -->` on its marker line,
  in its block or on the line before it,
  for example a single holistic judgment with no separable criteria.

A rubric the pull request does not touch is never reported.
With no base to diff against, the check skips
instead of scanning the whole tree.
It warns by default, because the rule is a default for most rubrics, not an absolute one;
`fail: true` makes it block.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | `*.qmd *.md` | Git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive) |
| `paths-ignore` | none | Comma or newline separated globs to skip |
| `fail` | `false` | Fail on a finding; `false` warns |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Scan every rubric, to measure a corpus |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version |

## Usage

Copy `examples/check-rubric-checklists.yml` to
`.github/workflows/check-rubric-checklists.yml`.
